name: set_gripper
description:
Set one or both grippers to a named directive in a single call.
Use when: you are opening to release or approach, or closing to grasp, and you already know which directive each gripper should hold. On a two-armed embodiment this is how the two are coordinated: naming both in one call is the only way to state that they change together. Near miss: this is not grasp_execute. If you have chosen a current grasp candidate and accept the committed sequence without intermediate decisions, call that instead -- it approaches, closes and measures as one committed sequence, and a bare close here does none of that. Use this standalone command when a separate decision after pose execution is needed.
Effect: submits one gripper directive per named gripper through the Supervisor and moves the jaws at a limited rate; an accepted command consumes one robot decision, and a refusal that executed no native actions and changed nothing consumes none. **An omitted gripper holds its current directive; it is not re-sent and not re-actuated.** The end-effector pose target is held unchanged. Measured state may still move under contact, and that is evidence rather than a fault.
Returns: the measured receipt and remaining_budget once the directive completes; the next observation follows with the current camera images. When closing, an intent block echoes the target_ref you supplied and labels it agent_annotation_only.
Does not: prove anything was grasped, held, released or moved; report jaw separation; verify what the jaws closed on; or make target_ref evidence -- it is your annotation of what you believe you are closing on, never a measurement. A closed jaw is not a grasp.
On error: Refused: an empty targets map or an arm outside left and right, or a directive other than open and close; a target_ref that is blank or not a string (invalid_arguments, naming target_ref); the episode's terminal boundary (episode_terminal). A schema refusal is invalid_arguments naming the field; an invalid_motion_arguments refusal names none -- re-read this schema rather than resubmitting the same shape. invalid_arguments naming target_ref means a blank string was sent; send a non-empty reference or omit it entirely. Timing: one native action is 10 physics steps of 4 ms (25 Hz, 40 ms per native action); one command uses at most 30 native actions (1.2 s). The drive target moves every physics step from where it was last commanded, never restarting from the fingers. A close moves at the SDK limiter's full drive, its target at most 10.8 mm (0.2 of the opening) ahead of the first finger's reading; once that finger moves less than 0.005 of the opening in one native action, the target leads it by at most 5 mm, which bounds the squeeze on an object. Before it starts, the command holds everything for up to 5 native actions until the arm moves slower than 0.05 rad/s, so the jaws do not close on an arm still converging from its last move; an arm whose measured joint velocities are already that slow costs none. An open moves at full drive, also when it releases a close. A close from fully open that meets nothing reaches the closed floor (normalized opening about 0.185) in about 5 native actions (0.2 s), and an open from closed takes about 6 (0.24 s). A command ends as soon as every named gripper is within 0.03 of its effective target, or has stopped short of it: two consecutive native actions that each moved less than 0.005 of the normalized opening. A close that stops on an object therefore ends 2 native actions (0.08 s) after the jaws stop, and reports not_reached with failure_code gripper_stalled_before_target and, for each named arm, arms.<arm>.gripper_outcome: state, commanded_opening_normalized, effective_target_opening_normalized, measured_opening_normalized (both fingers' mean), sdk_limited_drive_target_normalized (the drive target the jaws hold: at most 5 mm, about 0.09, below the first finger's reading after a close stops on an object), measured_finger_displacements_m, finger_lateral_offset_m, primary_finger_limit_holds_close (true when the close stopped with the second finger at that held target), ticks_used, ticks_budget and seconds_used. That is the expected result of closing on an object, not a controller fault. gripper_not_reached with state moving_at_budget means a jaw was still moving when the 30 native actions ran out. A stalled close is consistent with a grasp but does not prove one, and the normalized opening is not a calibrated jaw width: lift and observe to check retention. Fixed texts stated once here and left out of results and effects: the action effect's gripper_outcome.claim_boundary is "stalled_before_target means the jaws stopped short of the commanded opening; it is consistent with an object between the fingers and is not proof of a grasp". Controller arrival uses position error <= 0.01 m, orientation error <= 5.73 deg and normalized gripper error <= 0.03; the released primitives use at most 20 native actions per command and this one at most 30. Gripper feedback distinguishes requested directive, applied drive target, measured opening (both fingers' mean) and effective arrival target (the actual joint-limit floor for close). For explicit gripper commands, the SDK limits the applied target to within 0.2 normalized units of the current FIRST finger encoder, then derives both mimic drive targets from that limited value. Repeating close with an unchanged first-finger measurement does not request a more closed applied endpoint. A pose-only action holds the last APPLIED gripper target; it does not continue recomputing the close limiter. A blocked close can therefore remain a requested close while the applied target is intermediate; neither encoder arrival nor an intermediate target establishes contact or retention. Exact current targets, residuals and thresholds accompany observation and action feedback. Controller feedback contract: {"arrival_comparison":"<=","gripper_drive_limit":{"applies_to":"explicit_gripper_commands","coupling":"both_drive_targets_from_limited_primary_target","kind":"measured_primary_relative","maximum_normalized_offset":0.2,"pose_hold":"preserve_last_applied_drive_target","reference":"current_primary_finger_encoder"},"gripper_tolerance_normalized":0.03,"native_actions_per_command":20,"orientation_tolerance_deg":5.729578,"position_tolerance_m":0.01,"schema":"ora.controller-feedback.v1"}
The next observation does not repeat this receipt. Native action budgets are fixed offline and cannot be supplied as tool arguments.

targets.description: Which grippers change and to what. Name only the grippers you intend to change; an omitted one holds its current directive. Dimensionless named directives, not apertures.

left.description: Directive for the left gripper. Omit to hold. Null means omitted.

right.description: Directive for the right gripper. Omit to hold. Null means omitted.

target_ref.description: Optional annotation naming the target you believe you are closing on, from the current observation. Dimensionless reference; recorded and echoed, never treated as evidence that anything was grasped. Meaningless when only opening.
